title: The Colorful Note Surprise
markdown:
Once upon a time, at the bustling Harbor School, lived Edie the duck and Cas the cat. Edie had bright curious eyes. Every day she’d bounce with the dawn, but she often felt things were just a little too predictable. She yearned for sparklers and surprise parties. Cas, a sleek black cat, preferred to wake with quiet grace. He watched everything with a twitch of his whiskers, often imagining secret codes and daring rescues. Every day was much the same: lessons about tides and knot-tying, then watching the big ships bob in the water. Predictable. Comfortable.

Until one day, something quite peculiar started happening. A brand-new harbour messenger, a puffin with an impressively neat beak, began delivering notes. Not just any notes. Colour-coded. A bright yellow one. Then a deep blue. Then a vibrant green. And with each colourful scrap, rumours at Harbor School began to sparkle.

Edie’s eyes lit up like twin lighthouses. “A treasure map!” she quacked, convinced the yellow note meant a chest bursting with golden coins. Doubloons. Dazzling jewels under a tropical sun. Her feathers puffed with delight. Cas flicked his tail with a knowing air. “Nonsense, Edie,” he purred, whiskers vibrating. “That yellow must signify something far more important. A secret signal. Or a coded message from an undercover agent.” Shadowy figures on the docks. Whispered passwords. Daring escapades under the cloak of night.

The blue note arrived the next day. The paper felt cool against Edie’s beak. She declared it a map to a magical floating ice cream parlour, rainbow sprinkles and fizzy lemonade fountains. “Imagine!” A little happy dance. Cas, stretching languidly, countered that blue was the colour of the deepest oceans, clearly a sunken submarine, mysterious buttons and blinking lights. He pictured himself navigating its depths, cool water swirling.

Headmistress Plum, a sensible badger with spectacles perched on her nose and a perpetual air of calm, tried her best to keep things grounded. “Now, now, students. Let’s stick to facts, shall we? A note is simply a note.” Even she couldn’t quite suppress a small smile when the green note appeared, which Edie promptly translated as a ticket to a concert performed by singing seagulls, melodies sweeter than any seashell. Cas, naturally, suspected a blueprint for a brand-new super-fast silent gliding device. Zipping through the sky, wind ruffling his fur, faster than any bird.

The little harbour school buzzed with a delightful kind of energy. Edie would practise her spectacular diving techniques, convinced she’d need them to retrieve sunken treasure from the ocean floor. She’d imagine the feel of cool water and the glint of gold. Cas would spend his break times observing the pigeons, practising his stealth for a potential spy mission, flattening himself against the walls and moving with silent paws. Headmistress Plum found herself explaining the practical uses of a compass and the scientific principles of aerodynamics with extra vigour, just in case. The puffin messenger continued his deliveries, a blur of black and white, completely unaware of the spectacular tales unfolding in his wake, the flapping of his wings like a drumbeat to their growing excitement.

Then, one bright morning, a note arrived that was a riot of colour. Dazzling brilliant pink, almost as bright as the sunrise. Edie gasped, beak falling open. “This must be it! The ultimate discovery! A grand parade! Balloons bobbing like jellyfish, confetti raining like a sparkling shower, a giant magnificent cake topped with glowing cherries!” Cas leaned forward on his paws, eyes narrowed. “Pink. The colour of mystery. Instructions for a secret flying contraption. Perhaps one that can reach the moon.” The entire school gathered, little hearts thumping like tiny drums. The classroom practically vibrating with unanswered questions.

Until finally, Headmistress Plum, with a twinkle that hinted at a secret of her own, opened the dazzling pink note. A hush so quiet you could hear the gentle splash of waves and the faint rustle of papers. “My dear students. This note is not a map to treasure, nor a blueprint for a flying machine.” A collective gasp. Edie’s beak dropped even further. Cas’s tail went completely still. Then Plum held up the note so everyone could see its cheerful patterns. “It is an invitation. To a surprise party. For Eira the starfish, who has been feeling a little quiet lately. We’re having sea-berry tarts and singing our happiest songs.”

The whole school erupted in cheers, a wave of pure delight. The treasure was friendship and shared joy. The secret mission was kindness, and making someone feel happy. Edie and Cas, a little surprised their grand theories weren’t quite right, both agreed a party was indeed spectacular, perhaps even more so than gold or moon-missions. They helped decorate with colourful shells and long strands of seaweed. The happiest songs echoed across the harbour, mixing with gulls and the lap of waves. Eira the starfish, wiggling happily in a special little tank, glowed with delight, arms reaching out as if to hug them all.

Edie still dreamed up grand adventures, quacks brimming with possibility. Cas still pondered mysteries, keen eyes noticing every little detail. The most wonderful surprises, they found, often came in the simplest colourful packages — like a bright pink note — and a day filled with friendship, and tarts, and a starfish who was not quiet anymore.
characters: Edie (a duck), Cas (a cat), Plum (a headmistress)
